title: All 3-state 2-color Turing machines behave simply from blank tape

fields.label: Label
fields.value: All 3-state 2-color Turing machines behave simply from blank tape

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: With blank initial conditions all 2,985,984 Turing machines with 3 states and 2 colors quickly produce simple repetitive or nested behavior, and even with more complicated initial conditions their behavior eventually seems to resolve into a simple form.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: With 3 states and 2 colors it turns out that with blank initial conditions all of the 2,985,984 possible Turing machines of this type quickly evolve to produce simple repetitive or nested behavior.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “Universality in Turing Machines and Other Systems” (from p. 706), p. 710. Scope: 3-state 2-color Turing machines

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-31: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The blank-tape finite census is directly reproducible and strongly testable. Existing finite runs cannot resolve the claim over all more complicated inputs or all future times.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate all 2,985,984 machines from blank tape, simulate to a prespecified horizon, and detect halting, periodic, and nested traces. For nonblank inputs, sample or symbolically analyze explicit input classes and search for traces that fail to simplify.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Repetitive and nested need formal classifiers.

The set of complicated initial conditions is unbounded.

No finite horizon proves eventual simplicity.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The blank-tape half is a finite enumeration inside the reach of existing Turing-machine deciders, and it can be redone. The claim also says that more complicated inputs still resolve into a simple form, which a blank-tape census does not address. Samples of other inputs can support or weaken that half without covering it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run all 2,985,984 machines with 3 states and 2 colors from a blank tape and classify each as quickly periodic or nested. That census confirms or refutes the blank-tape sentence. The further sentence, about every more complicated initial condition, is tested only by sampling unless a proof covers all tapes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Quickly and simple need time and classifier cutoffs before the blank-tape census is unique.

There are infinitely many non-blank tapes, so examples that eventually simplify do not prove the universal claim.
